tex_statement:
Beyond the classical counting argument, we prove that forged
chains advance at half real-time speed, and light-client safety is
proved directly in a timed model, against an adversary that harvests
coerced signatures stamped for any slot, so the recency check is a
machine-checked safety ingredient --- and we develop key rotation inside
consensus against an adversary who steals keys and keeps them forever:
three rotation modes with exactly stated operator and client duties.

The payload (transactions, in a deployment) travels out of band;
\code{contentsHash} commits to it, and no consensus rule ever looks inside
it.

\code{keyIndex} is the version of the signing key the producer used:
key rotation is part of the consensus state, carried in band, and
Section~\ref{sec:results} builds on it.

\code{prev} is the parent's id, and \code{id} is a hash of
the block itself, computed and checked by the deployment's hashing layer
under a fixed contract:
\[
\mathit{id} \;=\; H(\mathit{slot},\ \mathit{height},\ \mathit{prev},\
\mathit{parentSig},\ \mathit{contentsHash},\ \mathit{keyIndex}).

A chain is a sequence of blocks with heights increasing by one, slots
strictly increasing, and each block linking to its parent's id, rooted
at a genesis block --- height zero, no parent (\code{linksOk},
\code{genesisOk}); that the root is the deployment's genesis is what
the theorems hypothesize (Section~\ref{sec:assumptions}).

A chain must be
\emph{dense} (\code{validChain} names the combined structure-and-density
checks): every matured window of $n$
consecutive slots must contain at least $\quorum$ blocks of the chain,
where a window $[u, u+n)$ has matured once the tip has reached its end,
$u + n \le \mathit{tip.slot} + 1$ (\code{denseSoFar}).

This counting
argument is the core combinatorial engine of every safety theorem in
Section~\ref{sec:results}, around which cryptographic unforgeability,
certificate grounding, and rotation pin mechanisms are layered and
machine-checked.
notes: High-level prose assertion summarizing formal results.

tex_statement:
Chain validity has one more condition, riding on the \code{keyIndex}
field: along the chain, a producer's declared key version never
decreases (\code{keyMonoOk}) --- rotation only ever moves forward, and
the chain's order is the agreed order in which rotations happen.

Structure, density, and this monotone rule together are
\code{validChainK}: \emph{the} chain validity of this paper.

The rules touch cryptography only through two small interfaces that a
deployment implements:
\begin{itemize}
\item \code{SigOps} --- $\mathit{sign}$ and $\mathit{verify}$ ---
  together with the versioned key map $\mathit{keyFor}(i,j)$, the
  public key of seat $i$'s signing key at version $j$ (a separate
  parameter, \code{KeyRegistry}, in the model; the implementation's
  dictionary folds it into \code{SigOps});
\item \code{CertOps} --- verify a certificate, read its claim, and
  extend it by one validated block; the implementation's dictionary
  (Section~\ref{sec:impl}) also exposes a by-tip-id lookup of locally
  held certificates, which compaction uses.
notes: Prose claim referencing Molt.SigOps, Molt.KeyRegistry, Molt.CertOps.

tex_statement: \paragraph{Validate} (\code{validCertifiedChain}).

Accept a certified
chain only if all of the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the certificate verifies (\code{CertOps.verify} --- one cheap check,
  e.g.\ of a recursive proof);
\item every suffix block's signature verifies under
  $\mathit{keyFor}(\text{slot's producer},\ \text{declared version})$;
\item the first suffix block extends the claim's tip: height one up, slot
  strictly later, \code{prev} equal to the tip id --- and every adjacent
  suffix pair links the same way;
\item every window that matures within the suffix is dense, counted over
  the claim's boundary buffer plus the suffix (\code{validSuffix});
\item the key-version discipline holds: a producer's declared versions
  never decrease (\code{keyMonoOk}, Section~\ref{sec:protocol}), and
  every block's declared version satisfies the deployment's rotation
  \emph{pin} (a floor in modes 1--2, exact per grid window in mode 3) --- the
  one mode-specific check, fixed at deployment.
notes: Prose claim referencing MoltPetit.Model.CertOps.verify, MoltPetit.Model.Block.prev, Molt.validSuffix, Molt.keyMonoOk.

\begin{assumption}[Signatures]\label{ass:sig}
Signing happens at real slots (\code{TimedExecution}).

The assumption
bundles: \emph{(a) custody} --- honest nodes sign only through their
honest signing path, and their secret keys never leave them; \emph{(b)
unforgeability} --- no one can produce a valid signature on a message the
key holder never signed, even after obtaining signatures on messages of
their own choosing (the standard EUF-CMA notion); here the attacker gets
exactly that power at every bad slot, whose producer can be made to sign
anything; and \emph{(c) the timed signing discipline} --- at a bad real slot
the producer's key signs arbitrarily many blocks with any stamp in its
residue class (\code{key\_match}); an honest real slot signs only its own
current block (\code{honest\_stamp}) and at most once (\code{honest\_once});
and every producer signature accepted by the verifier at real slot $R$
was produced at some real slot no later than $R$ (\code{hbridge},
causality plus EUF-CMA).

The id-formation contract of Section~\ref{sec:protocol} ensures that a block
is signed only once its parent is available (\code{chain\_order}).
\quad\textit{(Lean: \code{TimedExecution}, \code{hbridge}.)

\begin{assumption}[Hash collision resistance, over blocks that
occur]\label{ass:hash}
For the headline theorem, collision resistance holds over the blocks that
occur: any two blocks occurring in the execution with equal ids are
equal (\code{TimedExecution.id\_inj} over \code{SignedEver}).

We call this \emph{hash injectivity}; under rotation
the domain is version-stamped signed blocks --- for the chain-level
sync-rule results (Theorem~\ref{thm:refresh}), blocks verifying under
\emph{some} registered version of their producer (Lean
\code{KeyStealingSigned}); for the scheduled, lockstep, and certified
results it narrows to blocks verifying under their \emph{declared}
version (\code{SignedDeclared}), a strictly weaker assumption ---
Section~\ref{sec:protocol} explains why \code{keyIndex} is in the
preimage.
notes: Prose claim referencing Molt.KeyStealingSigned, Molt.SignedDeclared, MoltPetit.Model.Block.keyIndex.

tex_statement:
The light-client and timed results (Theorems~\ref{thm:lc}
and~\ref{thm:forge}) are carried to each implementation by that
implementation's soundness bridge (Section~\ref{sec:impl}), which also
covers the validator's key-discipline conjunct; the rotation-mode
results of Section~\ref{sec:rotation} and the liveness theorem are,

notes: High-level prose assertion summarizing formal results.
Theorem 1: headline timed light client safety.

tex_statement:
A block signed \emph{late}
--- at a real slot after its stamp --- can only come from a bad real slot,
and on a chain meeting the real-time recency bar such blocks form a tail
of at most $\fmax$ blocks inside one window (\code{late\_tail\_short}; the
same rate argument as Theorem~\ref{thm:forge}).

A third remark on the untimed model: the earlier result
\code{Molt.light\_client\_safety} reaches the same conclusion in an
untimed model, but it assumes the residue \code{SigUnforgeableRecent}
directly and keeps the exposure hypothesis.

The \emph{timed model}
(\code{TimedExecution}) adds a real-time axis: a log of what each real
slot's producer signed --- at an honest real slot, at most its own
current block; at a bad real slot, arbitrarily many blocks of the
adversary's choosing under that producer's key --- arbitrary content,
and stamped with any slot at all, not only the real slot at which the
signing happens.

The id-formation contract
of Section~\ref{sec:protocol} appears as the field \code{chain\_order}: a
block can be signed only once its parent is \emph{available}, because the
parent's id preimage contains the parent's signature, and predicting
another party's signature on a known message is exactly an EUF-CMA
forgery.

\begin{theorem}[Forged suffixes advance at half speed; Lean
\code{forged\_time\_bound}]\label{thm:forge}
In the timed model with the fault budget: let a valid chain be available
at real slot $r_{\mathrm{now}}$, let $F$ be one of its blocks, first
signed at real slot $r_0$, and let every chain block past $F$'s slot have
been signed only at bad real slots (the suffix above $F$ is forged by
coercion). Then
\[
\quorum \cdot \left\lfloor
  \tfrac{\mathit{tip.slot} - F.\mathit{slot}}{n} \right\rfloor
\;\le\;
\fmax \cdot \left( \left\lfloor \tfrac{r_{\mathrm{now}} - r_0}{n}
  \right\rfloor + 1 \right).
\]
Since $\quorum \approx 2\fmax$: forging a suffix that spans $s$ slots
takes about $2s$ real slots. The from-genesis corollary
(\code{forged\_chain\_time\_bound}) reads: a fully forged chain claiming
tip slot $s$ cannot exist before real slot ${\approx}\,2s$. (The Lean
statements carry non-degeneracy side conditions --- $n \ge 2$, $F$ not
the first block; a forged span under one window makes the
bound trivially true, ruling nothing out.)
\end{theorem}
notes: Theorem 2: forged suffixes advance at half speed.

tex_statement:
At real slot $r$ only $r$'s
producer's key can be made to sign, so two chain blocks first-signed at
$r$ belong to one producer and their slot stamps differ by at least $n$;
density puts some other seat's block between those stamps; and signing
order (\code{chain\_order}: a block cannot be signed before its parent
exists) forces that middle block's first signing back to $r$ as well ---
under a key that real slot cannot reach.

A fork meeting the
real-time recency bar has had too little real time to forge an $n$-deep
ancestor, and Theorem~\ref{thm:lc} is the machine-checked statement of
exactly that at staleness $n$.
notes: High-level prose assertion summarizing formal results.

tex_statement:
The protocol's key-rotation machinery was defined with the protocol
itself: the in-band version (\code{keyIndex}, Section~\ref{sec:protocol})
and the monotone rule (\code{keyMonoOk}) are already part of the one
chain validity.

The key-stealing corruption predicate
(\code{badKeyrot}) counts a slot bad if it is rented \emph{or} some
version at-or-above the one in force for its producer is stolen ---
which builds \emph{healing} into the definition: a stolen key stops
counting the moment its retirement takes force.

Hash injectivity (Assumption~\ref{ass:hash}) is consumed
alongside, its domain rescoped per mode: any-registered-version signed
blocks (\code{KeyStealingSigned}) for mode 1's chain-level rule,
declared-version signed blocks (\code{SignedDeclared}) for modes 2--3
and the certified mode-1 form.

Unlike the untimed residue \code{SigUnforgeableRecent} (Appendix~\ref{app:timed-uniq}), this is stated directly rather than derived: Appendix~\ref{app:timed-uniq}'s derivation needs only \emph{one} key's safety per real slot, while \code{KeyStealingEUFCMA}/\code{SchedCoreUnforgeable} are stated per individual key version, and one real slot can host several eligible key versions of which only one verifies --- so one key's safety does not certify the slot's, and the timed-model route does not generalize here without weakening an already-assumed primitive (machine-checked: \code{badSched\_single\_key\_safe\_not\_enough}, \code{badKeyrot\_single\_key\_safe\_not\_enough}).
notes: Prose claim referencing Molt.SigUnforgeableRecent, Molt.KeyStealingEUFCMA, Molt.SchedCoreUnforgeable, Molt.badSched_single_key_safe_not_enough, Molt.badKeyrot_single_key_safe_not_enough.

tex_statement:
With nothing stolen the
corruption the theorems count collapses to rent alone in every mode
(\code{badKeyrot\_lossOnly}, \code{badSched\_lossOnly}; mode 3 inherits
mode 2's count) --- no anchor, no cadence, any pin.

The pin
is read off the chain being validated: seat $i$'s version \emph{in force}
at slot $s$ (\code{inForce}) is the highest version $i$ has declared in
the chain's \emph{confirmed prefix} --- blocks at least $n$ slots old ---
and no block may declare less (\code{validSignedChainK$'$}).

notes: Theorem 3: client sync rule (timed confirmation depth and membership forms).

The anchor sits fewer than $2n$ \emph{slots} below that
tip although it is $n$ \emph{blocks} deep --- density leaves no room for
more (two full windows in the gap would demand $2\quorum > n$ blocks
where only $n$ exist; Lean \code{deep\_block\_span}).

First, it
asks for strictly less than the natural lifetime assumption: a
deployment that keeps $\rho + T$ within $\fmax$ on every window from
genesis onward satisfies the hypothesis outright, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:refresh} covers it as an immediate special case ---
and taking the
anchor to be the genesis block recovers the lifetime-budget statement

The agreement itself also holds at the
certificate presentation, with the floor --- the map sending each seat
to its version in force --- carried as a snapshot in the
claim --- the certificate must attest claim and floor \emph{together},
an unauthenticated floor readmits stolen retired keys
(\code{keyrot\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}, over the

trailing form as well: two certificate-plus-suffix presentations that
both contain the client's anchor agree $n$ deep, with the corruption

history the certificate could be attesting
(\code{keyrot\_certified\_suffix\_agreement\_anchored}; the client
rules at this presentation are \code{cert\_sync\_rule} and
\code{cert\_max\_sync\_period}).

\emph{Upward} (\code{max\_sync\_period}):
safety holds whenever rented slots plus the theft census stay within
$\fmax$ on every window starting in the trailing $F + 4n$ slots or
later.

\]
\emph{Downward} (\code{census\_accumulates},
\code{census\_accumulates\_later\_thefts}, \code{no\_budget\_beyond}):
the census at a window is \emph{at least} the number of distinct
producers with an ever-stolen version not yet retired there --- a theft

Together they confine what a theft
at real slot $r$ can expose to the slots $[r, r{+}d)$

The census a deployment attests is then per window and does not grow

Agreement with the honest chain itself follows by an induction over

sync's agreement keeps the next anchor on a reference chain that
grows over time, provided that chain's tip is at least as tall as the

The height comparison is a

The join checkpoint starts the induction as the op-model's fresh trust

\begin{theorem}[Scheduled safety under horizon budget; Lean
\code{sched\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_agreement\_horizon},\hfil\penalty0
\code{sched\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem\_horizon}]\label{thm:sched}
Under the scheduled validator (\code{validSignedChainSched}) on both
chains; the scheduled signature surface (\code{SchedUnforgeable},
recency-scoped with $\mathit{now}$, $\Delta$); hash injectivity over
declared-version signatures (Assumption~\ref{ass:hash}, \code{SignedHashInjective});
the corruption budget \code{ByzantineBoundedFrom}~$H$~$n$~(\code{badSched} \dots)
--- at most $\fmax$ bad slots in every $n$-slot window starting at or after
a horizon $H$; the horizon side conditions $H + n \le \mathit{tip}.\mathit{slot} + 1$
for both tips; recency $\mathit{now} \le \mathit{tip}.\mathit{slot} + \Delta$
for both tips; sufficient chain length $n < \mathit{length}$ (\code{hLong},
for both chains at equal heights; for the lower chain at unequal heights);
and the tip-height relation of each form (\code{hTipHeight}: equal
heights; \code{hLe}: the first tip no higher). Then two accepted chains agree: at equal tip heights, on the block $n$ below
each tip; at unequal tip heights, the lower chain's $n$-deep ancestor block
is a block of the taller chain, at least $n$ deep there.
There is no shared-genesis hypothesis: genesis agreement is a consequence
(\code{sched\_recent\_genesis\_agreement\_horizon}).
The global-budget \code{scheduled\_client\_safety} is the corollary at
any $H$ (\code{byzantineBoundedFrom\_of\_bounded}).
No anchor, no sync rule, no confirmation wait: the client holds a clock
and the constant $\mathit{gen}$, and may stay offline arbitrarily long.
\end{theorem}
notes: Theorem 4: scheduled safety under horizon budget (agreement and ancestor membership).

tex_statement:
Two of these
duties are \emph{named operational assumptions the cited theorems do
not consume}: \emph{not-before} --- a generation's key cannot be stolen
before it is derived; formalized separately as
\code{NoPrematureTheft} in the timed theft layer --- and
\emph{cold-root custody}, which stays informal.

No erasure is
required --- a retired key is harmless \emph{by rule}, not by secrecy: a
chain whose tip declares a generation whose era ended more than $n$
slots ago fails the recency check
(\code{sched\_oldkey\_fork\_stale}).

The statements carry to the
certificate presentation with no floor snapshot in the claim --- the
certificate state stays the plain one, each fold merely adding the pin
check --- since the pin is computed from each block's own slot (the
grounding \code{GroundedCertSched};
\code{sched\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}).

Through
Theorem~\ref{thm:sched} and the parent-id chain
(\code{same\_block\_same\_prefix}), any two accepted chains agree on the
whole confirmed prefix whatever happened while the wallet slept.

Only the
certificate form is proved under the global all-window budget, with the
strengthened grounding \code{GroundedCertSched}
(\code{sched\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}); carrying the
horizon scoping to certificates is future work.

The roster advances a single shared generation counter at
moments of its own choosing --- an incident, a governance decision ---
and validity enforces only the \emph{discipline} of the switch
(\code{noMixing}): within each grid window (slots $[Wn,\,Wn{+}n)$; the
fixed grid, not a sliding window) all blocks declare one generation, and
the counter never decreases across grid windows
(\code{validSignedChainLock}).

\begin{theorem}[Lockstep safety; Lean
\code{lockstep\_client\_safety}]\label{thm:lock}
Under the lockstep validator and the lockstep hypothesis package (the
roster tracks one monotone counter; honest signatures declare their
grid window's value; the genesis declares the counter's initial value; hash
injectivity; the same $\rho$/$T$ budget, assessed at the
one-grid-window-lagged counter over the pin-free core validator's signature
surface): the same anchor-free agreement as Theorem~\ref{thm:sched}, in
both forms (\code{lockstep\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem} at unequal
heights). The client holds even less than
mode 2's --- genesis and a clock, with no schedule to store at all.
\end{theorem}

The route is a machine-checked \emph{pinning} theorem
(\code{lockstep\_declares\_rosterGen}): on any accepted recent chain,
every matured grid window declares exactly the roster's counter --- a
grid window at any other generation would need a quorum of adversarial
blocks, which
a $\rho + T \le \fmax$ adversary cannot supply.

\begin{theorem}[Lockstep safety, per-generation census; Lean \code{lockstep\_client\_safety\_gen},\hfil\penalty0
\code{lockstepGen\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem}]\label{thm:lock-gen}
Under the lockstep validator (\code{validSignedChainLock}) and the
per-generation package --- honest signatures declare their grid window's
counter; hash injectivity; the pin-free core signature surface; rent at most
$\rho$ per window and, for every generation $j$ separately, at most $T$ seats
whose generation-$j$ key is stolen; $\rho + T \le \fmax$; recency
$\mathit{now} \le \mathit{tip.slot} + \Delta$ for both tips; and chain length
$2n < \mathit{length}$ (\code{hLong}, for both chains at equal heights;
for the lower chain at unequal heights) --- any two accepted chains agree:
at equal tip heights (\code{hTipHeight}), on the block $2n$ below each tip
(\code{lockstep\_client\_safety\_gen}); at unequal tip heights, the lower
chain's $2n$-deep block is a block of the taller chain, at least $2n$ deep
there (\code{lockstepGen\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem}).
Through the parent-id chain, they agree on their whole common prefix down
to height $0$: no shared genesis is assumed
(\code{lockstepGen\_recent\_genesis\_agreement}).
\end{theorem}

The route is a second pinning theorem that needs neither induction nor genesis (\code{lockstep\_window\_declares\_rosterGen}): the last grid window matured below the lower tip declares one generation on both chains, so the counting argument runs on a window whose corruption reading is at a single generation (\code{window\_shared\_prefix}).
The unmatured tip window cannot be used, and that is what costs depth $2n$ --- exactly $n + ((t{+}1) \bmod n)$ positions for lower tip slot $t$ (\code{lockstepGen\_shared\_prefix\_sharp}).
The two packages are incomparable in general; the cumulative one delivers the per-generation one when the counter skips no generation (\code{LockstepPackage.toGen}).

Its budget credit is now formal: with theft time-stamped, erasure is the hypothesis that no generation is stolen after the roster has moved past it (\code{ErasureTimedLock}), and it is \emph{consumed} --- it turns the census a deployment attests while a generation is live into the per-generation census Theorem~\ref{thm:lock-gen} needs (\code{genBound\_of\_preRetirementBound}; end to end, \code{lockstep\_client\_safety\_timed}).
notes: Prose claim referencing Molt.ErasureTimedLock, Molt.genBound_of_preRetirementBound, Molt.lockstep_client_safety_timed.

tex_statement:
The certificate carries the claim and the tip generation; for
$n \ge 2$ the generation is determined by the claim's own tail
(\code{groundedCertLock\_gen\_of\_tail}, \code{groundedCertLock\_gen\_unique}),
so the certificate attests nothing beyond the plain claim, and only
$n = 1$ needs the extra counter --- which must then be attested with
the claim: an unauthenticated counter readmits a stolen retired-generation
key exactly as an unauthenticated floor does in mode 1.

What must then be
true of the world: the core surface over the pin-free validator and hash
injectivity (the adversary paragraph's rescopings); the standing clock
assumption (Assumption~\ref{ass:clock}); the coordination discipline above (a
silent split among honest signers is an operational failure outside the
theorems); and \emph{either} the same $\rho$/$T$ budget as mode 2's
global form, assessed at the one-grid-window-lagged counter
(Theorem~\ref{thm:lock}, depth $n$), \emph{or}, at confirmation depth
$2n$, rent at most $\rho$ per window and, for every generation $j$, at
most $T$ seats whose generation-$j$ key is stolen while $j$ is live
(Theorem~\ref{thm:lock-gen}; end to end with time-stamped theft,
\code{lockstep\_client\_safety\_timed}).

Conclusion, machine-checked (\code{lockstep\_client\_safety} and
\code{lockstep\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem}, via the pinning theorem
\code{lockstep\_declares\_rosterGen}; and at the certificate presentation under
the cumulative budget at depth $n$,
\code{lockstep\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}, with the
certificate's own counter pinned to the roster's once its grid window
matures, \code{lockstep\_cert\_gen\_pinned}): any two accepted chains agree ---
at equal heights on the block $n$ below each tip (or $2n$ for full chains under
Theorem~\ref{thm:lock-gen}), at unequal heights the
lower chain's confirmed block lying on the taller --- hence, through the
parent-id chain (\code{same\_block\_same\_prefix}), on the lower chain's
whole confirmed prefix --- with no schedule anywhere and no anchor.
notes: Prose claim referencing Molt.lockstep_client_safety, Molt.lockstep_recent_tip_ancestor_mem, Molt.lockstep_declares_rosterGen, Molt.lockstep_recent_certified_suffix_agreement, Molt.lockstep_cert_gen_pinned, Molt.same_block_same_prefix.

tex_statement:
First, while the timed theft layer (\code{theft\_exposure\_window}) confines
exposure to $[r, r{+}d)$ under the asserted hypothesis \code{NoTheftBackdating}
and frees $F$ from retroactive census growth
(\code{paced\_tight\_census\_bound\_all\_F}), there is no execution-level
separation between the timed and untimed budgets
(\code{paced\_budget\_holds\_under\_timing}): the gain is in the operational
assumptions a deployment must defend, and deriving no-theft-backdating from
mint-timed signature primitives remains future work.
notes: Prose claim referencing MoltPetit.Model.theft_exposure_window, Molt.NoTheftBackdating, Molt.paced_tight_census_bound_all_F, Molt.paced_budget_holds_under_timing.

tex_statement:
Second, while mode~3 formalizes per-generation erasure credit at depth $2n$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:lock-gen}), both mode~2's certificate theorem
(\code{sched\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}) and mode~3's certificate
theorem (\code{lockstep\_recent\_certified\_suffix\_agreement}) are proved under
cumulative/global fault budgets at depth $n$; carrying horizon scoping to mode-2
certificates and per-generation erasure credit to mode-3 certificates at depth $2n$
remain future work.

Third, the per-mode signature surfaces are not derived from the timed model:
as witnessed by \code{badSched\_single\_key\_safe\_not\_enough} and
\code{badKeyrot\_single\_key\_safe\_not\_enough}, single-key safety does not
imply slot safety, so per-mode no-back-dating is stated directly as an
operational assumption (Assumption~\ref{ass:rotation-honest}).

\begin{theorem}[Liveness; Lean \code{production\_liveness},
\code{global\_liveness}]\label{thm:live}
\emph{Local:} under the fault budget and honest delivery
(Assumptions~\ref{ass:budget} and~\ref{ass:delivery}), when a slot
arrives that belongs to an honest producer holding an accepted chain,
production succeeds --- the extension passes the same validator everyone
runs. \emph{Global:} a synchronous honest run within the budget (over
the run's span; each honest block reaches the next honest producer
within its slot) is
validator-accepted with one block per honest slot, so the chain reaches
any height and every block eventually becomes $n$-deep.
\end{theorem}
notes: Theorem 7: liveness (local production and global liveness).

tex_statement:
The Lean
development proves a threshold that is sufficient, and necessary over
the pipeline's steady states
(\code{slot\_time\_sufficient}, \code{slot\_time\_necessary}); we do not
reproduce the formula here --- Section~\ref{sec:impl} instantiates it at
the measured proving costs.

From
it:
\begin{itemize}
\item \emph{The native validator} is imported into Lean and proved sound
  against the model: if the extracted code accepts a chain, the semantic
  predicate holds (\code{rust\_valid\_chain\_sound} and companions).

Soundness is the only direction safety needs --- completeness is a
  liveness concern --- and it is what carries Theorems~\ref{thm:lc}
  and~\ref{thm:forge} to the shipped code
  (\code{rust\_recent\_tip\_ancestor\_mem}, and under the timed model and
  certificate bridge, \code{Rust.rust\_timed\_certified\_agreement}).

The bridges cover the
  validator's structural core and its key-discipline conjunct
  (\code{rust\_valid\_chain\_sound}, \code{rust\_valid\_chain\_k\_sound});
  the three rotation \emph{pins} of Section~\ref{sec:rotation} are,
  today, stated and checked at model level.

\item \emph{The circuit} instantiates the same source's backend-generic
  validator (\code{valid\_chain\_be}) over plonky2, so the recursive
  certificate proves exactly the predicate that was verified
  (\code{valid\_chain\_be\_validChain}); the per-gadget faithfulness of
  the circuit backend is the one remaining trust assumption, stated
  rather than proved.

First, \emph{consensus is free}: the
machine-checked validator adds no appreciable proving cost on top of
whatever the application already pays for signatures.

} Beyond the trusted base of
Section~\ref{sec:impl} --- the Lean kernel; the pinned translation
front-ends (Charon + Aeneas, Thales), including the hand-audited
emitter-bug corrections in the vendored TS emission; and the per-gadget
faithfulness of the circuit backend, stated rather than proved (the
equivalence lemma \code{valid\_chain\_be\_validChain} is proved at the
native u64 instantiation) --- everything not machine-checked is a named
hypothesis standing next to the theorem that consumes it: the operational
assumptions of Section~\ref{sec:assumptions}; the key-stealing signature
surface (assumed, not derived from the timed model, and, precisely, cannot
be by the technique of Appendix~\ref{app:timed-uniq} without weakening the
surface's per-key premise; Assumption~\ref{ass:rotation-honest} records the
resulting operational content directly instead); version independence
of keys under theft (instantiable with key-insulated
signatures~\cite{keyinsulated}); the circuit path's out-of-circuit trust
anchor (the roster commitment to the cold roots); and the recency check
itself, which lives in the unverified node loop since the pure validators
carry no clock --- threading $\mathit{now}$ through them is mechanical
future work; and the per-mode operational assumptions of
Section~\ref{sec:rotation} (not-before and cold-root custody; lockstep
coordination and erasure; the mode-1 reaction delay).

One of these is
not yet in its final form: mode~1's reaction delay (\code{Reacts}) is
stated about the version in force \emph{on the chain being validated},
so a deployment discharges it by rotating promptly but cannot check it
ahead of time for chains it has not seen; a form quantified only over
the honest chain is open.

The headline Theorem~\ref{thm:lc} does not use this residue or
\code{NoBackdate}.

Rather, this appendix shows the route by which the
untimed model's residue \code{SigUnforgeableRecent} (used in
\code{light\_client\_safety}) follows from EUF-CMA plus no back-dating.

A
projection connects them (\code{projectSigned}): a producer's entry for
stamped slot $s$ is the block \emph{stamped} $s$ that it signed \emph{at
real slot} $s$, its own slot --- single-valued at an honest slot because
an honest node signs at most once per slot (at a bad slot the entry is
an arbitrary choice the theorem never consults).

Two hypotheses then
close the gap:
\begin{itemize}
\item the \emph{EUF-CMA bridge}: a verifying signature was produced at
  \emph{some} real slot --- with no constraint on which;
\item \emph{no back-dating} (\code{NoBackdate}): a block whose stamp is
  an honest slot was signed \emph{only} at the real slot equal to its
  stamp.

notes: Theorem 8: untimed residue derived in timed model.

tex_statement:
The second clause is the whole content --- the bare timed model does allow
a bad real slot to mint a block stamped for one of its producer's
honest slots, and we machine-check exactly such an execution
(\code{noBackdate\_independent}, at $n = 2$): every timed-model field
holds, no-back-dating fails.

The per-mode key-stealing surfaces of Section~\ref{sec:rotation} are not
instances of Theorem~\ref{thm:timed-uniq}: their EUF-CMA hypothesis is stated
per key version, one level finer than this appendix's per-real-slot corruption
predicate, and a real slot can be safe for one key while unsafe for another
eligible one at the same slot --- see Assumption~\ref{ass:rotation-honest}
(machine-checked: \code{badSched\_single\_key\_safe\_not\_enough},
\code{badKeyrot\_single\_key\_safe\_not\_enough}).
